title: Genetic variants shape single-cell chromatin accessibility and disease risk
title_zh: 遗传变异塑造单细胞染色质可及性和疾病风险
abstract: Understanding how genetic variation shapes gene regulation at single-cell resolution is crucial for elucidating complex disease mechanisms1, but has been limited by the lack of large-scale single-cell multi-omics data2–4. Here we present single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing of 3.5 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 1,042 donors with matched whole-genome sequencing. Across 28 immune cell types, we tested 440,996 chromatin accessibility peaks and identified 243,225 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) at 100,483 peaks, 60% of them cell-type specific. Rare variant analysis identified 38,161 associated peaks, with predicted transcription factor-binding disruption implicated at individual loci. Colocalization with expression QTLs (eQTLs) from single-cell RNA sequencing data (5.4 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells)5 defined 28,834 candidate cis-regulatory elements. Across genome-wide association studies for 16 diseases and 44 blood traits, caQTLs colocalized 4.5–22.6% more signals than eQTLs alone. Cell-type-specific and tissue-specific context, distal effects and multi-causal-variant models raised genome-wide association study–eQTL concordance from approximately 16% to approximately 65%. Cell state further modulates genetic effects, with 27% of over 200,000 caQTL–cell-state interactions lacking a main effect. At the inflammatory bowel disease risk gene ADCY7, accessibility effects varied with genotype and G protein-mediated pathway activity in CD4+ T cells. A graph neural network trained on both eQTL and caQTL layers inferred peak–gene links in unpaired multiome data with up to 17.2% higher accuracy than QTL-agnostic data, uncovering 128 additional transcription factor–target pairs (22% increase). Together, these results show that genetic variants shape chromatin accessibility in a cell-type-specific and cell-state-specific manner, influencing immune function and disease risk. Single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling identifies cell-type-specific and cell-state-specific genetic effects that link non-coding variants to immune disease risk.
abstract_zh: 理解遗传变异如何在单细胞水平塑造基因调控对于阐释复杂疾病机制至关重要，但此前受限于缺乏大规模单细胞多组学数据。本文呈现了来自1042名供体（匹配全基因组测序）的350万个外周血单个核细胞的转座酶可及染色质测序单细胞分析。在28种免疫细胞类型中，我们检测了440996个染色质可及性峰，并鉴定出100483个峰上的243225个染色质可及性定量性状位点（caQTLs），其中60%具有细胞类型特异性。罕见变异分析发现了38161个相关峰，个别位点的转录因子结合位点破坏被预测有关。与单细胞RNA测序数据（540万个外周血单个核细胞）中的表达定量性状位点（eQTLs）共定位，界定了28834个候选顺式调控元件。在16种疾病和44种血液性状的全基因组关联研究中，caQTLs共定位的信号比单独eQTLs多4.5%至22.6%。细胞类型特异性和组织特异性环境、远端效应以及多因果变异模型将全基因组关联研究与eQTL的一致性从大约16%提高到大约65%。细胞状态进一步调节遗传效应，在20万个caQTL–细胞状态相互作用中，27%不存在主要效应。在炎症性肠病风险基因ADCY7处，可及性效应随CD4+ T细胞中G蛋白介导通路活性和基因型而变化。在同时基于eQTL和caQTL层训练的图神经网络，推断未配对多组学数据中的峰–基因关联，准确度较不考虑QTL的数据高出最多17.2%，发现了128个额外的转录因子–靶点对（增加22%）。这些结果共同表明，遗传变异以细胞类型特异性和细胞状态特异性的方式塑造染色质可及性，影响免疫功能和疾病风险。单细胞染色质可及性分析可鉴定与非编码变异相关的免疫性疾病风险的细胞类型特异性和细胞状态特异性遗传效应。
